predecessors.name: Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro
predecessors.text: the prince-bishopric that Danilo I gave up on 13 March 1852 ('gave up his position as prince-bishop and married')

ledger.x: 13 March 1852: Danilo I secularises the prince-bishopric and Montenegro becomes a principality.
May 1858: Montenegro wins at Grahovac and the border is redrawn.
13 July 1878: the Treaty of Berlin ends the war.
13 July 1878: independence recognised and the territory doubles.
28 August 1910: the principality becomes a kingdom.
1912: Montenegro joins the First Balkan War.
30 May 1913: Montenegro and Serbia split the Sanjak of Novi Pazar.
May 1913: the war with the Ottomans ends for Montenegro with the loss of Shkodër and the split of the Sandzak (30 May 1913); the Treaty of London is not named on the page opened.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest confirms Metohija.
October 1918: the Austro-Hungarian occupation ends ('from 15 January 1916 to October 1918').
26 November 1918: the Podgorica Assembly deposes Nikola and votes union with Serbia.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)
Serbia and Montenegro (Federal Republic of Yugoslavia)

wars.name: Battle of Grahovac
wars.outcome: Montenegrin victory in May 1858; the Great Powers demarcated the border and Montenegro gained Grahovo, Rudine and other areas.

wars.name: Montenegrin-Ottoman War (1876-1878)
wars.outcome: Independence recognised and the territory grown from 4,405 to 9,475 km2 (Treaties of San Stefano and Berlin, 13 July 1878).

wars.name: First Balkan War
wars.outcome: Montenegro gives up Shkodër to Albania (May 1913), splits the Sandzak with Serbia (30 May 1913) and receives Metohija by the Treaty of Bucharest (10 August 1913).

wars.name: Austro-Hungarian occupation of Montenegro
wars.outcome: The kingdom is occupied from 15 January 1916 to October 1918 and does not return: the Podgorica Assembly votes union with Serbia on 26 November 1918.

certainty.note: The mountain frontier with the Ottomans was not demarcated; the page gives no border.
After Grahovac 'the Great Powers then demarcated the border'.
The Treaty of Berlin frontier; Ulcinj's handover and the Plav-Gusinje question are not on the pages opened.
Balkan War fronts: Scutari and the Sanjak change hands monthly; the Treaty of Bucharest (10 August 1913) fixes the Metohija line.
The 1913 frontier with Serbia and Albania.
Montenegro is not a state in these years (part of Yugoslavia and then Serbia and Montenegro); no shape is drawn.
